title.narrative: Community-Based Ebola Prevention and Preparedness Response in Ituri and North Kivu, DRC

description.narrative: The project is expected to improve community knowledge, trust and adoption of practical Ebola prevention measures in targeted areas of Ituri and North Kivu. It will focus on communities at heightened risk of transmission, particularly households living near confirmed or suspected cases in Bunia and Rwampara, and high-risk communities in Karisimbi, Goma affected by population movement, displacement and limited access to trusted health information. The project will prioritise those most at risk and furthest behind, including women and girls, displaced households, carers, people with disabilities, older people, children and adolescents reached through schools and community spaces, and households with limited access to hygiene materials or reliable Ebola prevention information. Targeting data will be disaggregated by sex, age and vulnerability wherever possible through registration, training attendance, distribution lists, KAP monitoring, PDM and community feedback mechanisms. Expected results include: - 48 frontline health staff, including nurses and health facility staff, trained on Ebola prevention, IPC-related measures, risk communication and safe alert / referral messaging through agreed health structures. - 90 community leaders, community health workers, including relais comunautaire, and religious leaders trained to support trusted community messaging, community sensitisation, address rumours and misinformation, and promote early health-seeking behaviour. - Approximately 70,200 people directly reached through community awareness sessions in churches, schools, markets and other public locations with information on Ebola prevention, symptoms, hygiene practices and where to seek support. - Approximately 445,000 people indirectly reached through radio and mass communication with key Ebola prevention and preparedness messages. - 1,450 high-risk households in Bunia and Rwampara provided with hygiene kits to support improved household-level prevention practices. - 600 women and girls provided with dignity kits, where appropriate, as part of a protection-sensitive approach to supporting affected and at-risk communities. - 48 handwashing stations installed in public locations in Bunia and Rwampara to support improved hygiene practices and reduce transmission risk. Together, these results will contribute to improved awareness, reduced misinformation, strengthened community trust in the wider Ebola response, and increased adoption of practical prevention behaviours in targeted high-risk communities.
